name: Srimad Bhagavad Gita
description: The Bhagavad Gita ("Song of God") is a 700-verse Hindu scripture, part of the epic Mahabharata (Bhishma Parva, chapters 23–40). Set on the battlefield of Kurukshetra, it is a dialogue between Prince Arjuna and his charioteer, Lord Krishna, an avatar of Vishnu. It is a foundational text of Hinduism that serves as a guide for ethical living, duty, and spiritual liberation.

ar_cards.title: Overview
ar_cards.body: Bhagavad Gita is a sacred Hindu scripture and a part of the Mahabharata. It contains a conversation between Lord Krishna and Arjuna, offering guidance on life, duty, and spirituality.

ar_cards.title: Origin
ar_cards.body: The Bhagavad Gita originated in Kurukshetra, Haryana, India, where Lord Krishna imparted its teachings to Arjuna before the great Mahabharata war.

ar_cards.title: Author and Language
ar_cards.body: The text is traditionally attributed to Sage Vyasa and was composed in Sanskrit. It consists of poetic verses that convey profound philosophical ideas.

ar_cards.title: Structure
ar_cards.body: The Bhagavad Gita contains 700 verses divided into 18 chapters. Each chapter focuses on different aspects of yoga, devotion, knowledge, and righteous action.

ar_cards.title: Significance
ar_cards.body: The Bhagavad Gita teaches the importance of performing one's duty without attachment to results. Its timeless wisdom has influenced philosophers, leaders, and spiritual seekers worldwide.

name: Thirukural
description: Thirukkural is an ancient Tamil masterpiece authored by Thiruvalluvar, consisting of 133 chapters and 1330 couplets. It is divided into three sections: Aram (Virtue), Porul (Wealth), and Inbam (Love), covering various aspects of human life. The work promotes moral values, good governance, and harmonious relationships, making it relevant across cultures and generations.

ar_cards.title: Overview
ar_cards.body: Thirukkural is a classical Tamil literary work written by the poet-philosopher Thiruvalluvar. It is one of the most respected texts in Tamil literature and provides guidance for ethical living.

ar_cards.title: Origin
ar_cards.body: The Thirukkural originated in ancient Tamil Nadu, India. Thiruvalluvar is traditionally associated with Mylapore (Chennai), though the exact place of composition is uncertain.

ar_cards.title: Period and Author
ar_cards.body: The work was authored by Thiruvalluvar and is believed to have been composed around the 1st century BCE to 1st century CE, approximately 2,000 years ago.

ar_cards.title: Structure
ar_cards.body: The Thirukkural consists of 1330 couplets (Kurals) arranged into 133 chapters. It is divided into three sections: Aram (Virtue), Porul (Wealth), and Inbam (Love).

ar_cards.title: Significance
ar_cards.body: The Thirukkural promotes moral values, good governance, social harmony, and personal discipline. Its universal teachings have made it one of the most translated and celebrated works of Tamil literature.

name: Wooden Buddha Sculpture
description: This wooden sculpture depicts Gautama Buddha in a calm and meditative posture, symbolizing enlightenment, wisdom, and inner peace. The intricate carving highlights the craftsmanship of traditional artisans and the spiritual significance of Buddhist art.
curator: Crafted from wood, this artifact reflects the artistic traditions of Buddhist communities and demonstrates how religious beliefs were expressed through sculpture and decorative craftsmanship.

ar_cards.title: Overview
ar_cards.body: Buddha Sculpture depicts Siddhartha Gautama, the founder of Buddhism. Such sculptures symbolize peace, wisdom, enlightenment, and compassion.

ar_cards.title: Historical Period
ar_cards.body: This sculpture belongs to the Buddhist artistic tradition, which flourished in India from the 3rd century BCE onward. Different styles emerged during periods such as Gandhara, Mathura, and Gupta.

ar_cards.title: Material and Craftsmanship
ar_cards.body: Buddha sculptures were commonly carved from stone, bronze, marble, or wood. Artists paid special attention to facial expressions, posture, and symbolic hand gestures (mudras).

ar_cards.title: Symbolism
ar_cards.body: The sculpture's features carry deep meaning. The lotus position represents spiritual purity, while hand gestures such as Dharmachakra Mudra or Abhaya Mudra symbolize teaching, protection, and fearlessness.

ar_cards.title: Cultural Significance
ar_cards.body: Buddha sculptures are important religious and cultural artifacts. They serve as objects of meditation and devotion and reflect the spread of Buddhist philosophy and art across Asia.

name: Bronze Ganesha Statue
description: This bronze statue depicts Lord Ganesha, the Hindu deity of wisdom, prosperity, and the remover of obstacles. The sculpture showcases fine metal craftsmanship, intricate ornaments, and traditional iconographic features associated with Ganesha.
curator: Bronze Ganesha sculptures are significant examples of South Indian temple art. They reflect the advanced bronze-casting techniques of ancient artisans and highlight the cultural and religious importance of Ganesha worship.

ar_cards.title: Bronze Ganesha Statue
ar_cards.body: This bronze statue represents Lord Ganesha, one of the most revered deities in Hinduism, known as the remover of obstacles and the patron of wisdom.

ar_cards.title: Material
ar_cards.body: Crafted from bronze using traditional lost-wax casting techniques, the statue demonstrates exceptional metallurgical and artistic skill.

ar_cards.title: Origin
ar_cards.body: The sculpture originates from Tamil Nadu, a region renowned for its rich tradition of bronze icon-making and temple art.

ar_cards.title: Symbolism
ar_cards.body: Ganesha's elephant head symbolizes wisdom and intelligence, while his large ears represent attentive listening and learning.

ar_cards.title: Cultural Significance
ar_cards.body: Bronze Ganesha statues are commonly used in temples and homes for worship and are important symbols of faith, prosperity, and auspicious beginnings.

name: Wooden Jagannath Statue
description: This wooden statue depicts Lord Jagannath, a revered form of Lord Vishnu worshipped primarily in Odisha. The sculpture is characterized by its distinctive large eyes, vibrant appearance, and unique artistic style, reflecting centuries of devotional tradition.
curator: Wooden Jagannath statues are central to the religious and cultural heritage of Puri. They represent the rich traditions associated with the Jagannath Temple and the world-famous Rath Yatra festival.

ar_cards.title: Overview
ar_cards.body: This wooden statue represents Lord Jagannath, a form of Lord Vishnu worshipped by millions of devotees across India, especially in Odisha.

ar_cards.title: Material
ar_cards.body: Traditionally carved from sacred wood, Jagannath statues are renowned for their distinctive craftsmanship and symbolic design.

ar_cards.title: Origin
ar_cards.body: The statue originates from Puri, Odisha, home to the famous Jagannath Temple and one of Hinduism's most important pilgrimage sites.

ar_cards.title: Symbolism
ar_cards.body: The large circular eyes symbolize divine vision and omnipresence, while the simplified form represents the universal and accessible nature of the deity.

ar_cards.title: Cultural Significance
ar_cards.body: Lord Jagannath is deeply associated with the annual Rath Yatra (Chariot Festival), a major religious event that attracts millions of pilgrims and visitors from around the world.
